chunks: The Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, informed me from Abu al-Qasim Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father, from Sa'd ibn 'Abd Allah, from Abu Ja'far, from Muhammad ibn Abi 'Umayr, from Hammad ibn 'Uthman, from 'Ubayd Allah ibn 'Ali al-Halabi, from Abu 'Abd Allah عليه السلام, that he said:

If you do not know whether you have prayed four or five, or whether you have decreased or increased, then recite the tashahhud and give salām, and perform the two sajdahs of forgetfulness without ruku' and without recitation, and recite in them a light tashahhud.

key_terms.تَشَهَّدْ: recite the tashahhud formula in prayer
key_terms.تَشَهُّدًا خَفِيفًا: a brief tashahhud recited in the two sajdahs of forgetfulness
key_terms.خَمْسًا: five rak'ahs in salat (prayer), indicating possible addition
key_terms.رُكُوعٍ: the bowing act in salat (prayer), which is not done in these sajdahs
key_terms.سَجْدَتَيِ السَّهْوِ: the two prostrations performed for forgetfulness or uncertainty in prayer
key_terms.سَلِّمْ: give salām to conclude the prayer
key_terms.قِرَاءَةٍ: recitation, which is omitted in the sajdahs of forgetfulness

ai.seo_question: What should a person do in salat (prayer) if they are unsure whether they prayed four or five rak'ahs?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling for one who becomes uncertain in salat (prayer) about whether they prayed four or five rak'ahs, or whether they omitted or added something. It instructs the person to complete the prayer with tashahhud and salām, then perform the two sajdahs of forgetfulness with a light tashahhud and without ruku' or recitation.
